treatise.fmab.start.title: First steps
treatise.fmab.start.welcome:
Welcome, apprentice.

This Treatise goes with you from your first chalk stroke to the secrets of the Gate. This chapter walks you through your first transmutation, step by step: follow it, chalk in hand.

The arrows at the bottom turn the pages; "Contents" takes you back to the list of chapters. Greyed-out chapters will open on their own as you progress: hover over one in the contents to see when.
treatise.fmab.start.kit:
What you already have.

- This Treatise.
- The Rudiments tome, whose glyphs you already understand: Earth, Water, Fix, Project.
- Transmutation chalk.
- A circle notebook you keep in your head (N key). It holds three ready-made circles: a stone wall, a spike and an ice platform.

You have nothing to draw to get started.
treatise.fmab.start.choose:
Step 1: choose the circle.

The chalk always draws the circle selected in the notebook. At first, that is the stone wall: you can go on to step 2.

To change it later, hold R: the circle wheel opens. Point at a circle and release. Scroll to go from one wheel of nine circles to the next; hold right click to put a circle wherever you like. Or open the notebook (N), turn its pages and click "Save": the open page becomes the one the chalk draws.
treatise.fmab.start.draw:
Step 2: draw.

Find a clear spot, on grass, dirt or stone. Face the place where the wall should rise: the circle keeps the direction you were looking in.

Chalk in hand, right-click the top of a block on the ground. The circle is drawn there.

Sneaking, a right-click on empty air changes the size of the circles the chalk draws.
treatise.fmab.start.palm:
Step 3: lay your palm.

Put the chalk away: you need an empty hand. Right-click the circle.

A wall five blocks wide rises two steps away, made of the earth dug just in front of it. Nothing comes from nothing: that is equivalent exchange.

Well done: you are an alchemist now.
treatise.fmab.start.trouble:
It did not work?

- "Your hand must be free": put away what you are holding.
- "Not enough concentration": the blue gauge above your hunger is empty. Wait, sneaking: it comes back faster.
- "Not enough matter": the wall takes the earth, sand or stone just in front of it; on wood or water, it has nothing to take.
- The circle is gone: rain washes chalk away. Draw it again.
- "Rebound!": the circle was badly composed (see "Mistakes and rebounds").
treatise.fmab.start.practice:
Practise.

Take the spike (R wheel) and draw it facing a monster: it bursts out three steps away and throws it back.

Take the ice platform and draw it on a riverbank: the water around freezes, and you walk across.

Each successful transmutation raises your mastery: little by little you will understand the glyphs you draw, and new chapters will unveil themselves.
treatise.fmab.start.next:
What next?

- "Everyday circles": mining, crossing, trapping monsters, running redstone, repairing your tools. Each circle goes into the notebook in one click.
- "The three steps" and "Composing a circle": how a circle works.
- "Thinking a circle through": inventing your own.

Before you draw, the notebook (N) tells you whether a circle will work.
treatise.fmab.everyday.title: Everyday circles
treatise.fmab.everyday.p1:
Alchemy, day to day.

This chapter answers a survivor's needs: shelter, crossing, mining, defence, running a contraption. Each page shows a working circle: "Add to notebook" copies it, then you only have to draw it.

Some glyphs come from another tome than the Rudiments: without the tome, the circle goes off but may rebound. Those marked (Alchemist) waver until you reach that rank.
treatise.fmab.everyday.night:
The first night.

Night falls and you have no shelter? Back against a cliff, draw the stone wall (already in your notebook) facing the danger: five blocks wide rise two steps away.

Turn and do it again: in a few circles, you are dug in. Each wall takes its earth just in front of it, and the ditch it leaves slows attackers down.
treatise.fmab.everyday.river:
Crossing a river: Water and Fix in a triangle (Rudiments).

Draw it on the bank: the water around the circle, up to three blocks out, freezes into ice. Walk onto the ice, draw it again further on: step by step, a bridge.

Intensity dots on the ring widen the ice (see "Thinking a circle through").
treatise.fmab.everyday.mine:
Mine shaft: Earth and Decompose in a square, two Intensity dots (On Stone and Metal; Handbook of Forms).

Stone, dirt and gravel break apart five blocks across and three deep, around the block that bears the circle: that one stays in place, like a pillar. The resources fall onto the circle.

Without the dots, the hole is three blocks across.
treatise.fmab.everyday.bridge:
Stone bridge (Alchemist): Earth and Air fused in a hexagram, with Fix (Notes on Combustion).

Draw it at the edge of the void, the river or the lava, and lay stone or dirt on the circle: a deck three wide runs eight blocks out from the circle, level with the ground. It is built from what you laid, then from your bag; it stops when matter runs out.

Draw it again at the end of the bridge to go further. A direction arrow picks the way.
treatise.fmab.everyday.tunnel:
Tunnel (Apprentice): Earth and Decompose in a square, a direction arrow on the ring (On Stone and Metal; Handbook of Forms).

On the floor, a three-by-three tunnel sets off at ground level the way the arrow points, eight blocks long: the stone, the dirt and the ores it holds fall onto the circle.

On a wall, no arrow needed: the tunnel goes through the wall that bears the circle. On a ceiling, it goes up. Two Intensity dots lengthen it by eight blocks.
treatise.fmab.everyday.harvest:
Harvest: Plant and Decompose in a square (On Living Matter).

Draw it in the middle of the field: everything ripe within four blocks is harvested and falls onto the circle. Wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroots, nether wart and cocoa are replanted with one of their seeds; sugar cane, cactus and bamboo are cut above their foot; melons and pumpkins picked off their stem, berries off their bush.

What is not ripe stays: draw it again next season.
treatise.fmab.everyday.growth:
Fertiliser: Plant and Project in a square (On Living Matter).

Crops, saplings, cocoa and berries within three blocks of the circle grow at once, as under bone meal. Each plant costs one: lay it on the circle, or keep it in your bag.

A Philosopher's Stone in hand needs no bone meal: a single soul grows everything in the area to maturity, and saplings become trees.

With the Harvest in series behind it, a single circle grows and then reaps.
treatise.fmab.everyday.leveling:
Earthworks (Alchemist): Earth and Air fused in a hexagram, with Decompose (Notes on Combustion).

The ground is levelled with the floor that bears the circle, seven blocks across: bumps of stone and dirt are planed down six blocks high, and their matter fills the hollows three deep. What is left falls onto the circle; what is missing comes from the circle or your bag.

The ideal ground to build on, or for a field.
treatise.fmab.everyday.switch:
Copper switch: Copper and Fix in a triangle (On Stone and Metal).

A redstone block appears for ten seconds in front of the circle: the iron door, lamp or piston touching it switches on.

Set as a trap (sneaking, bare-handed, right-click), it goes off when a creature walks on it: an arrow dispenser against the block, and your door defends itself. Stay close: it draws on your concentration.
treatise.fmab.everyday.repair:
Repairing your pickaxe: Iron and Repair in a square (On Stone and Metal).

Lay the worn iron tool or weapon on the circle, with iron ingots: each ingot restores a quarter of its durability. No anvil needed.

Everything an anvil repairs mends this way, with the element of its material and Repair: Wood for wood and shields, Earth for stone, Copper, Iron, Gold and Netherite for their metals, Carbon for diamond, Fiber for leather, Flesh for the elytra, Lime for turtle scute. Lay the material with the item.
treatise.fmab.everyday.recycling:
Woodcutter: Wood and Decompose in a square (On Wood and Fiber).

Draw it at the foot of the trees: every tree with a trunk within four blocks of the circle falls whole, and its logs roll onto the circle. The leaves stay and wither, sowing their saplings. A log cabin or a beam, with no leaves that grew on their own, does not move.

Lay a spare wooden item on the circle (chest, fence, boat…): it comes apart into its matter, and you learn how it is made (see "The three steps").

A second stage in series, Wood and Recompose, and the logs come out as planks.
treatise.fmab.everyday.aims:
Choosing the target (Alchemist): the Item, Block and Creature glyphs on the ring (Handbook of Forms).

The woodcutter takes apart the axe laid on the circle and fells the trees around, both at once. Add the Item's hook on the ring: it only recycles items, those on the circle and those lying on the ground within reach, and leaves the trees standing. The Block's staircase does the opposite: it fells, and leaves the axe alone. This holds for every circle that touches both items and the world: harvest, earth decomposition, tunnel.

The Creature's eye adds what the circle does to creatures: Water and Fix freeze them, Fire and Decompose set them ablaze, Plant and Project make the young grow up, Flesh and Repair heal. Each glyph weighs on the ring: you need one more side to the polygon.
treatise.fmab.everyday.furnace:
Furnace without a furnace (Alchemist): Fire and Decompose in a square (Notes on Combustion).

Lay on the circle what needs cooking (raw ores, raw meat, sand…) and some coal: it all cooks at once, eight items per coal, as in a furnace.
treatise.fmab.everyday.trap:
Monster trap (Alchemist): Earth and Project in a square, one Targets glyph on the ring (Handbook of Forms).

Set as a trap, it goes off when a zombie or a creeper steps on it: the spike bursts out in front of the circle, and another under the nearest creature. Draw it in front of your door, with the chisel so it lasts.
treatise.fmab.everyday.firebreak:
Firebreak (Alchemist): Air and Project in a hexagon, one Cone glyph on the ring (Notes on Combustion; Handbook of Forms).

A gust fans out in front of the circle: it puts out flames and pushes back what it touches. Against a forest fire, or an approaching horde.
treatise.fmab.everyday.habits:
Good habits.

- Rain washes chalk away: for a circle that must last (by the door, at the bottom of the mine), use alchemical paint, or the chisel on stone and metal.
- Keep some concentration to flee: one circle too many, and night catches you empty.
- On a wall, the effect goes straight out from it: a spike bursts from the wall.
- Village librarians sell tomes: each adds glyphs to your catalogue.
treatise.fmab.ch1.title: Principles and equivalent exchange
treatise.fmab.ch1.p1:
Alchemy is the science of understanding matter, breaking it down and building it back up.

Its absolute law is equivalent exchange: to obtain, something of equal value must be given. Nothing is made out of nothing.
treatise.fmab.ch1.p2:
Every material belongs to a family: mineral, metal, organic or crystal. A transmutation never changes family, and the mass produced never exceeds the mass given.

Stone gives stone, iron gives iron. A wall rises from the earth dug out in front of it.
treatise.fmab.ch1.p3:
Amestris.

Central City, the capital, is a great round walled city in the plains. North of its square stands the army headquarters: the State examiner awaits candidates there, in the courtyard that serves as an arena.

Resembool is a country hamlet. The Rockbell house holds an automail workshop.
treatise.fmab.ch2.title: The three steps
treatise.fmab.ch2.p1:
1. Comprehension: know the structure of matter. Alchemy tomes teach the glyphs; village librarians sell them. You also come to understand them by drawing them. A glyph you do not understand still works, but the circle may rebound.

2. Deconstruction: the target matter is broken down.

3. Reconstruction: it is rebuilt as the circle dictates.
treatise.fmab.ch2.p2:
In practice:
- Open your Circle Notebook (N key), draw your circle and save it.
- Trace it on the ground with Chalk (right-click the top of a block).
- Lay your palm on it: right-click, empty-handed.

Crouching, empty-handed, right-click a circle you do not have to copy it into your notebook.
treatise.fmab.ch3.title: Glyph catalogue
treatise.fmab.ch3.p1:
The following pages show each glyph. Copy them into the notebook with the Line, Circle, Polygon, Arc and Dot tools; a glyph you understand can be placed in one click with the Stamp tool.

Draw them upright (15° of tilt at most), large enough (at least 5 cells) and without letting them touch: two strokes that brush each other belong to the same glyph.
treatise.fmab.ch4.title: Composing a circle
treatise.fmab.ch4.p1:
The ring: a large circle centered on the page (Circle tool, start from the center, radius of at least 5 cells). Without a ring, nothing happens.

The polygon: Polygon tool, from the center out to the ring, so that every corner touches it. An Apprentice holds a triangle or a square; beyond that, the circle loses stability.
treatise.fmab.ch4.triggers: An inscribed circle normally goes off under the palm. Sneaking, bare-handed, a right-click changes its trigger: delayed (it goes off three seconds after the palm, time to step away), trap (it goes off when a creature steps on it, except you), or on a redstone signal. Whoever sets the trigger becomes its author: when the circle goes off on its own, it consumes their concentration and knowledge; if they are away, the circle fizzles out.
treatise.fmab.ch4.fusion: Two go further: if a second alchemist lays their palms on the same inscribed circle less than a second and a half after the first, their energies merge. The transmutation is nearly twice as strong, and costs them only half their concentration.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p2:
Inside: one element glyph (the matter) and one action glyph (what is done with it).

On the ring: Intensity dots (+50% range each) and a Direction arrow. Without an arrow, the effect goes where you are looking; the top of the page is the direction you faced while drawing.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p3:
Complexity: the sum of the glyphs. An Apprentice can hold 6; beyond that, as with the stages, sides, polygons and satellites their rank allows, the circle loses stability. A glyph above your rank takes some away too.

Stability: a stage bears as much complexity as its polygons have sides (2 for a bare ring), a quarter more if the glyphs are laid out symmetrically. Below 100%, the circle rebounds.

Concentration: every glyph costs some. It comes back with rest, faster while crouching.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p4:
Alchemist circles — stages.

Draw a second ring around the first: each ring is a stage, read from the center outwards. An Alchemist can hold two.

An outer stage only receives energy if a stroke running from one ring to the other links it to the previous one.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p5:
Links.

Single stroke: in series. The outer stage acts after the other, only if it succeeded, and can use the matter it produced.

Double stroke (two close parallel strokes): in parallel, each on its own.

Broken stroke (several aligned segments): conditional, the stage only acts if the previous one found nothing.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p6:
Satellites: a small circle (radius 2.5 to 5 cells) centered on a corner of the polygon.

With an element alone, it infuses the stage: Fire sets alight what the effect hits, Water slows, Air pushes back. Any other element alone infuses the stage too; some formulas require several (see “The Gate of Truth”).

With an element and an action, it casts its own effect, on the side of its corner. An Alchemist can place two.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p7:
Fusion: two elements in the same stage only combine within a hexagram (two inscribed triangles, one pointing up, one down).

Polygons can be layered: a stage bears the sum of their sides. An Alchemist layers three, a hexagram counting as two.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p8:
Knowledge.

Every successful transmutation raises the mastery of its school. Schools open node by node: cheaper concentration, more range, thick walls, transmuted weapons. The "Knowledge" button on the contents page shows where you stand.

An experienced enough Apprentice becomes an Alchemist: they hold two stages, the hexagon and two satellites without wavering.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p9:
Surfaces.

Chalk draws anywhere but washes away in the rain. Alchemical paint lasts. The chisel engraves forever, but only stone and metal.

Circles go on floors, walls or ceilings. On a wall or a ceiling, the effect goes straight out from the surface: a spike bursts from the wall, a wall rises in front of it.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p10:
Gloves.

At an alchemist's table, glove in hand, embroider the circle selected in your notebook (alchemical thread) or engrave it on a gauntlet (chisel). Use the glove to put it on.

G casts its circle on the surface you aim at, hand free; Shift+G joins hands and casts both. Spark gloves act at range, gauntlets when striking.
entity.fmab.stone_golem.rebuilt: The golem rebuilds itself: its circle still holds.
exam.fmab.intro: State Alchemist examination. First prove your mastery: a successful two-stage circle, then these items; the trial then awaits you in the arena.
exam.fmab.not_eligible: The State examination is open to Alchemists: you become one at 60 mastery points, by succeeding at transmutations. Come back when you are one.
exam.fmab.already_passed: You are already a State Alchemist. Wear your watch with honour.
exam.fmab.ready_to_fight: Items received. The trial: a stone golem bound to an engraved circle. As long as the circle holds, it gets back up.
exam.fmab.req.weapon: A transmuted weapon: stone lance (Earth) or arm blade (Metal), unlocked at 45 mastery or by the training fight against Izumi. Near the examiner, it does not crumble
exam.fmab.two_stages_proven: Two-stage circle succeeded: the State examiner will take it into account.
exam.fmab.items_accepted: The examiner accepts your items. On to the trial.
exam.fmab.arena_busy: A trial is already under way.
exam.fmab.no_room: There must be clear, flat ground in front of the examiner.
exam.fmab.fight_start: The engraved circle lights up: the golem awakens.
exam.fmab.passed: You are now a %s. Here is your watch.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p11:
The State examination.

An Alchemist may present themselves to the army examiner. They prove their mastery with a successful two-stage circle and items they hand over, then face in the arena a stone golem bound to an engraved circle: as long as the circle holds, the golem gets back up. Break the circle, then the golem.

The State Alchemist's watch lengthens your effects and spares your concentration.
block.fmab.alchemist_table.embroidered: The notebook's circle is now embroidered on the garment.
block.fmab.alchemist_table.needs_ink: A soul has no blood left: tracing its seal takes alchemical ink.
block.fmab.alchemist_table.no_seal: Select in your notebook the blood seal to trace: yours (Treatise, “The Gate of Truth”) or a friend's.
block.fmab.alchemist_table.sealed: The seal is traced inside the breastplate. Set it on an armor stand, above a soul circle.
tattoo.fmab.title: Tattoo ritual
tattoo.fmab.intro: The circle drawn on the ground will pass into the skin. The ritual hurts. A tattooed palm is cast like a glove; elsewhere, the circle acts permanently (the same effect only counts three times across all worn circles).
tattoo.fmab.occupied: This spot already bears a tattoo.
tattoo.fmab.erase_needs_ink: Erasing a tattoo takes %s alchemical inks in hand.
treatise.fmab.ch4.p12:
Worn circles.

A circle embroidered on a leather garment (one stage) or tattooed anywhere but the palms acts permanently: Earth and Fix reinforce, Water and Fix ward off fire, Air and Project lighten your step, Iron and Repair close wounds, Earth and Project sting whoever strikes you.

The same effect only counts three times, however many circles carry it; and near Father, none of them answers.

The tattoo: draw the circle on the ground, then use alchemical ink on it.
treatise.fmab.ch4.hold: Keep your hand on the circle after activating it: the energy keeps flowing. A wall rises, a spike grows longer as long as there is matter to take; a jet of flame or a gust repeats. Each moment costs a little concentration.
treatise.fmab.ch5.title: Circles to copy
treatise.fmab.ch5.p1:
Each page shows a working circle. "Copy drawing" puts its code on the clipboard: in the notebook, "Import" copies it in.

Redrawing it yourself is better, though: that is how one learns. “Thinking a circle through” teaches how to design your own.
treatise.fmab.ch5.wall:
Stone wall: Earth and Fix in a triangle.

A wall five blocks wide rises two steps from the circle, made of the earth dug out right in front of it.
treatise.fmab.ch5.spike:
Stone spike: Earth and Project in a triangle.

A spike bursts out three steps away and throws whatever stands there.
treatise.fmab.ch5.blade:
Iron blade: Iron and Project in a square.

Takes two iron ingots (laid on the circle or carried). Iron and Project weigh 4: a triangle could not hold them.
treatise.fmab.ch5.ice:
Ice platform: Water and Fix in a triangle.

Draw the circle by the water's edge: the water around it freezes.
treatise.fmab.ch5.decompose:
Decomposition: Earth and Decompose in a square.

The earth and stone around the support break down into resources.
treatise.fmab.ch5.repair:
Repair: Iron and Repair in a square.

Lay a worn iron tool and some iron on the circle: each ingot restores a quarter of its durability.
treatise.fmab.ch5.wide_wall:
Widened wall: the stone wall with two Intensity dots on the ring.

Dots weigh too: it needs a square.
treatise.fmab.ch5.series_spikes:
Spikes in series (Alchemist): in the center, Earth and Decompose; outside, Earth and Project, linked by a single stroke.

The stone broken down by the first stage forms the spike of the second.
treatise.fmab.ch5.fallback_wall:
Plan B (Alchemist): in the center, Water and Fix; outside, Earth and Fix, linked by a broken stroke.

By the water, it freezes; far from water, a wall rises instead.
treatise.fmab.ch5.burning_blade:
Burning blade (Alchemist): Iron and Project in a hexagon, and a Fire satellite on a corner.

The forged blade sets alight whatever it strikes.
treatise.fmab.ch5.amplified_combustion:
Amplified combustion (Alchemist): Fire, Air and Project in a hexagram layered with a hexagon.

The hexagram fuses both elements; the hexagon adds its six sides to bear the load. Burns two pieces of fuel.
treatise.fmab.ch5.detonation:
Detonation (Alchemist): Fire, Sulfur and Decompose in a hexagram layered with a hexagon.

The block under the targeted surface, four steps away, becomes a charge and blows up. The school of Explosion, Kimblee's.
treatise.fmab.ch5.more:
Other combinations, to work out yourself: smelting (Fire + Decompose: the circle's fuel cooks what lies on it), the flame jet (Fire + Project), the gust (Air + Project), the ice spike (Water + Project) and the ice wall (Water + Air + Fix, in a hexagram, "Ice wall" node).

Every matter glyph (Wood, Fiber, Carbon, Crystal, Sulfur, Lime, Plant, Flesh, the metals) breaks down and recomposes the objects of its element, with Decompose and Recompose.
treatise.fmab.ch5.stone_lance:
Stone lance (Alchemist, "Stone lance" node): Earth and Recompose in a square.

Two blocks of earth or stone under the circle become a lance, which comes straight to your hand.

If you think of an object (J key) or lay one as a model, the circle recomposes it instead.
treatise.fmab.ch5.arm_blade:
Arm blade (Alchemist, "Arm blade" node): Iron and Recompose in a square.

An iron ingot becomes a blade sharper than a sword; you get it back when the blade comes undone. With an automail arm, the arm itself is transmuted: a blade springs from the forearm, no ingot needed; the same transmutation draws it back in.

If you think of an object (J key) or lay one as a model, the circle recomposes it instead.
treatise.fmab.ch6.title: Mistakes and rebounds
treatise.fmab.ch6.p1:
A circle that does not react: no ring, no action or no element. Nothing is spent.

A circle beyond your rank reacts, but it wavers: every limit it exceeds takes away some stability, and it rebounds all the harder. A Philosopher's Stone holds it.

A glyph you do not understand lets the circle react, but each one adds a quarter chance of rebound. The notebook shows its verdict before you pick up the chalk.
treatise.fmab.ch6.p2:
A circle that rebounds: a polygon too weak, glyphs that do not combine, or an unreadable drawing. The energy comes back at the alchemist, in proportion to the mistake.

A circle with no chance at all blows up its support.
treatise.fmab.sealed.rank: This chapter will unveil itself at the rank of %s.
treatise.fmab.sealed.mastery: This chapter will unveil itself at %2$s mastery points (you have %1$s).
treatise.fmab.design.title: Thinking a circle through
treatise.fmab.design.p1:
This chapter gives no circles: it teaches how to design them. A good circle is thought out before it is drawn, in five questions.

1. What do you want to achieve?
2. On what matter, and to do what with it?
3. How heavy is it?
4. Which polygon bears it?
5. How should its glyphs be laid out?
treatise.fmab.design.p2:
1 and 2. Start from the effect.

A circle always answers two questions: which matter to act on (the element glyph), and what to do with it (the action glyph).

Fix raises and sets: a wall, a platform. Project throws: a spike, a blade. Decompose breaks into resources. Repair restores what is worn.

A passage to block? Earth and Fix. A river to cross? Water and Fix. A chipped tool? Iron and Repair.
treatise.fmab.design.p3:
3. Count before you draw.

Add up the complexity of each glyph: the catalogue gives it on its page. Earth, Water and Fix weigh 1; Iron, Project, Decompose and Repair, 2. On the ring, each Intensity dot and the Direction arrow weigh 1 too.

That total is the circle's load. An Apprentice bears 6 at most; beyond that, their circle wavers.
treatise.fmab.design.p4:
4. Choose the polygon.

A polygon bears as much load as it has sides: a triangle 3, a square 4 (a bare ring, 2). This is the measure that matters most: a circle heavier than its polygon rebounds.

Earth and Fix weigh 2: a triangle will do. Iron and Project weigh 4: it takes a square.

A polygon beyond your rank (more than four sides for an Apprentice) costs more stability than it brings: in their hands, a hexagon holds less than a square.
treatise.fmab.design.p5:
5. Lay out the glyphs: symmetry.

Glyphs laid out symmetrically let the polygon bear a quarter more: a triangle 3.75, a square 5.

Each glyph needs its reflection (the same glyph) on the other side of an axis through the centre, vertical or horizontal, or opposite it, by a half turn. A glyph placed on the axis is its own reflection: the simplest is to line yours up, one above the other.

The dots and the arrow, set on the ring, do not count here.
treatise.fmab.design.ice_bridge:
Wide ice bridge, step by step.

The effect: an ice platform that reaches far. The matter, Water; the action, Fix: load 2. Two Intensity dots for reach: load 4.

A symmetric triangle bears 3.75: too little. A symmetric square bears 5: it holds, with room to spare. Water and Fix are lined up on the axis.
treatise.fmab.design.aimed_spike:
Aimed spike, step by step.

Earth and Project (load 3), one Intensity dot and a Direction arrow: load 5, exactly what a symmetric square bears. One more glyph, and it would need a polygon an Apprentice cannot hold.

The arrow, on the right of the ring, sends the spike towards the right of the page: the top of the page is the direction you were facing while drawing.
treatise.fmab.design.p6:
Check, then try.

Draw the circle in the notebook first: it gives its verdict (stability, rank required, glyphs not yet understood) before you pick up the chalk. Below 100% stability, remove a glyph or take a bigger polygon.

In the field, a circle that does not react lacks a ring, an element or an action; a circle that rebounds is too heavy, badly combined or badly drawn (see “Mistakes and rebounds”). Change only one thing at a time: that is how you learn what went wrong.
treatise.fmab.stages.title: Thinking in stages
treatise.fmab.stages.p1:
Your rank of Alchemist opens this chapter to you. You now bear a load of 14, two stages, the hexagon, three layered polygons and two satellites.

When an idea no longer fits in a polygon, do not reach for the biggest one first: ask whether it is really two effects. Each stage bears its own load, and the circle is only as good as its weakest stage.
treatise.fmab.stages.p2:
The price of a stage.

A second stage doubles the concentration of the whole circle: each glyph costs as many times as there are stages, and reach is paid for on top.

A stage is only worth it if it brings one more effect. To strengthen a single effect, an Intensity dot or a bigger polygon costs less.
treatise.fmab.stages.p3:
Choosing the link.

Does the outer stage need what the other produces? Single stroke, in series: the stone decomposed at the centre becomes the spike outside.

Two independent effects, cast together? Double stroke, in parallel: each acts on its own.

A backup plan? Broken stroke, conditional: the outer stage only acts if the first found nothing, like the wall that rises far from water, instead of the ice.
treatise.fmab.stages.bristling_rampart:
Bristling rampart (Alchemist): at the centre, Earth and Fix; outside, Earth and Project, joined by a double stroke.

Both stages act together: a wall rises two steps away, a spike bursts out at three. In series, the spike would wait for the wall to succeed; in parallel, it goes off even if the wall found no earth.
treatise.fmab.stages.p4:
Satellite or stage?

A satellite holding a lone element infuses the stage without adding one: Fire sets alight what the effect touches, Water slows, Air pushes back. For a blade to burn, no second stage is needed: a Fire satellite on a corner is enough, and the concentration is not doubled.

A satellite holding an element and an action casts its own effect, on the side of its corner.

Its glyphs weigh in the stage's load: count them.
treatise.fmab.stages.p5:
Fusion and layering.

Two elements in the same stage only combine within a hexagram: it counts as two polygons and bears 6.

A heavier load? Layer polygons: the stage bears the sum of their sides. Fire, Air and Project weigh 8: the hexagram alone (7.5 when symmetric) is not enough; doubled with a hexagon, it bears 12. That is the amplified combustion in “Circles to copy”.

The shape glyphs (Circle, Cone), Duration and Targets go on the ring, like the dots, and weigh 1 each.
treatise.fmab.stages.hunting_spikes:
Hunting spikes (Alchemist): Earth and Project in a square, two Targets glyphs on the ring.

The spike bursts out in front of the circle, and another under each of the two nearest creatures. Load 5: the symmetric square is full.

Think about shape too: the Cone fans flames and gusts out over a crowd in front of you; the Circle sends them all around, when you are surrounded.
treatise.fmab.stages.p6:
Designing in two stages, step by step.

1. Draw the centre stage alone, and check it in the notebook.
2. Add the second ring, its polygon and its glyphs.
3. Join the two rings with the link you chose: without a stroke, the outer stage stays silent.
4. Count again: the two stages together must not exceed 14, and each must fit in its polygon.
5. Watch the concentration: a circle that drains it leaves you nothing for the next one.
treatise.fmab.mastery.title: Master circles
treatise.fmab.mastery.p1:
As a State Alchemist, your circles change scale: a load of 25, three stages, up to the dodecagon, six layered polygons and four satellites.

A great circle is not a small circle with more on it. Think of it as a machine: a main effect, what prepares it, what extends it, and what replaces it if it fails.
treatise.fmab.mastery.p2:
Give each stage a role.

The centre prepares: it decomposes, it supplies the matter. The second stage acts: it projects, it fixes. The third extends the effect, or replaces it: in series, it acts after the second; through a broken stroke, it only goes off if the second found nothing.

Each link is chosen from one ring to the next: the first and second stages can be in series, the second and third in parallel.
treatise.fmab.mastery.p3:
Place and timing.

A circle meant to last is engraved with the chisel, in stone or metal: the rain does not wash it away. Then choose its trigger (sneaking, bare-handed, right-click): delayed to step away, trap for whoever walks on it, redstone to tie it into your contraptions. It then draws on your concentration: far from you, it fizzles out.

On a wall or a ceiling, the effect goes straight out from the surface: a wall rises opposite, a spike bursts from the wall.
treatise.fmab.mastery.p4:
A circle for every use.

On the ground, there is no hurry: the great three-stage circle belongs there. In combat, there is no time to draw: embroider one-stage circles on your gloves, light on concentration.

What you want all the time is worn: embroidered on leather or tattooed, a one-stage circle toughens you, guards against fire or lightens your step.

Together, palms laid on the same circle at once make it nearly twice as strong, for half the concentration.
treatise.fmab.mastery.p5:
Beyond your rank.

A Philosopher's Stone holds the circles your rank cannot bear. But each transmutation costs it one soul, plus one per stage: a three-stage circle consumes four. Do not count on it to save a badly thought-out circle.

Knowledge, finally, lightens your circles: the nodes of each school lower concentration and lengthen reach. Build your great circles in the schools you master best.
treatise.fmab.ch7.title: Taboos
treatise.fmab.ch7.p1:
Two transmutations are forbidden.

Gold: State law punishes whoever makes it.

Human beings: without a Philosopher's Stone, no one has ever succeeded. Those who tried saw the Gate, and Truth took its toll.

This Treatise will say no more.
treatise.fmab.ch7.chimera: The chimera: place two beasts in a Human + Flesh + Decompose circle (a hexagram fuses the two elements), and they recompose into a single creature that obeys you (it follows you, hunts monsters, defends its master). That is the school of Life, and a taboo: karma collapses. Alkahestry, for its part, trains the school of Medicine; Scar's arm and decomposition, that of Destruction.
treatise.fmab.ch8.title: The Gate of Truth
treatise.fmab.ch8.p1:
Human transmutation: the Human glyph and Recompose, in a circle sized for a State Alchemist: below that rank, it wavers and rebounds, unless a Philosopher's Stone holds it. The circle writes out the full formula of a body: six satellites, one per element (Water, Carbon, Lime, Sulfur, Iron, Crystal for silicon). If one is missing, the circle rebounds.

On the circle lie the ingredients of a body: a bucket of water, eight coal, four bone meal, two glowstone dust, two gunpowder, an iron nugget and a quartz. The blood, the alchemist gives.

Without a Philosopher's Stone, it always fails.
treatise.fmab.ch8.human:
Human transmutation (State Alchemist): Human and Recompose at the heart of a hexagram inscribed in a dodecagon; on its six points, the satellites of the formula. A double ring surrounds it. No treatise reproduces this circle: you work it out yourself, or find it in very rare forbidden research notes (Laboratory 5's archives, the ruins of Xerxes, forgotten libraries).

Do not draw it.
treatise.fmab.ch8.p2:
What is born of the circle is nothing human. The alchemist is dragged to their Gate, in the White Space, where Truth takes its toll: an arm, a leg, the organs, the sight. The more was attempted (extra ingredients, humans in the circle, past openings), the heavier the price.

If an ingredient is missing, Truth takes the whole body.
treatise.fmab.ch8.p3:
In exchange, the alchemist has seen the Gate, and what lies behind it: they come back understanding every glyph. They join their hands (Shift + gloves key): the circle selected in their notebook acts on the surface they aim at, without chalk. The circle wheel (R, held) switches circles in one gesture; a left click on the wheel joins the hands at once. It takes two hands.

Every new opening costs a new toll.
treatise.fmab.ch8.p4:
A lost arm or leg is replaced with automail: standard iron, Rush Valley light steel (faster, more fragile) or the Briggs winter model (against frost). It is fitted at an automail bench or by Winry, in Rush Valley. It wears out; worn out, it stops responding, and Winry repairs it for iron.

Without legs, you crawl; or you sit in a wheelchair, crafted or bought from a toolsmith: two arms to turn the wheels, or someone to push it.
treatise.fmab.ch8.soul:
Soul circle (Alchemist): Human and Fix, in a hexagon. Lay an armor on the circle (on an armor stand or on the ground): it calls the soul whose seal the breastplate bears; bare, it calls the armored soul that activates it (which changes armor and leaves the old one standing), or else the soul that has wandered the longest.

Crouching at the alchemist table, you trace your seal inside a breastplate, with alchemical ink or your own blood. Set on an armor stand above a soul circle, it waits: a wandering soul asks its Truth to call it back there.

Another's soul does not come back for nothing: you must have seen your Gate, draw a human transmutation under the armor and offer a piece of yourself (an arm, a leg, your sight, your organs). Wandering souls are called from the oldest to the newest; you see the one that accepts before you pay.

What the Gate took from another can be given back: with an ally standing in a human transmutation, you pay with your own soul (the Truth takes your whole body, you wake up in an armor) or with souls from your Stone, at the same price as before the Gate. To a soul bound in an armor, only its body can be given back: you pay with your soul, with a Stone's souls, or with your Gate, like Edward for his brother, and you never perform alchemy again.
treatise.fmab.ch8.seal:
Your blood seal: it belongs to you alone. Add it to the notebook, select it, then, crouching at the alchemist table, trace it inside a breastplate (alchemical ink or your blood).

Share its code with a friend: they will be able to trace your seal for you.
treatise.fmab.ch9.title: The Homunculi
treatise.fmab.ch9.p1:
Homunculi are artificial beings. Their heart is a Philosopher's Stone, and each bears the Ouroboros tattooed somewhere on their body.

As long as the Stone holds souls, they do not die: they reconstitute on the spot, and the Stone wears out. The paler the red flesh that reforms them, the fewer souls they have left. At the last one, only a Stone core remains, and only the first time you bring down each kind of homunculus. Four cores fused around crystallized blood make a Philosopher's Stone of a hundred souls: whoever left something at the Gate uses it to take it back. The organs cost 15 souls, a leg 20, an arm 25, the sight 30, the whole body 60.
treatise.fmab.ch9.p2:
Lust: her fingers stretch into blades that pierce everything in a straight line, shields included. She pauses before striking: that is the moment to step aside. Fire burns her twice as much.

Gluttony: slow, he sucks in everything around him and swallows whoever comes near his mouth. In his Belly, kill what prowls, transmute to tear its wall open, or hold on until he spits you out.
treatise.fmab.ch9.p3: Lust and Gluttony guard Laboratory 5: a ruined guardhouse, and beneath it the hall where the army made Stones. A ladder shaft leads down. Like all of Father's servants, they only go after those who threaten Father's plans: whoever strikes them, carries a living Stone, refused his offer, saw one of them fall or sealed a blood crest. Everyone else, they ignore.
treatise.fmab.ch9.p4: Envy takes on the looks of anyone: a friend, a townsperson, yourself. Beware of whoever comes too close. Unmasked, he leaps; his Stone half empty, he becomes a monster made of faces; at the end, he is only a small lizard running away. Defeated once, he no longer comes to haunt you; still disguised, he leaves if no one comes near.
treatise.fmab.ch9.p5: Greed runs the Devil's Nest. His Ultimate Shield makes him invulnerable, except when he lowers it to strike. He does not look for a fight: offer him gold, emeralds or diamonds, or beat him twice, and he will fight at your side, as long as you pay him every day.
treatise.fmab.ch9.p6: Sloth digs an endless tunnel under Central. The strongest and fastest of them, but so lazy: he sighs, then rushes straight ahead, smashing through rock. After his charge, he catches his breath: strike then.
treatise.fmab.ch9.p7:
Führer King Bradley is Wrath. He has only one life, but his Ultimate Eye sees blows coming: he dodges arrows and half the blows struck from the front. Hit him in the back, or while he strikes.

His son Selim is Pride. His shadows cut and devour, but live only with light: plunge the room into total darkness, or flood it with light, and he is just a child.
treatise.fmab.ch10.title: The Philosopher's Stone
treatise.fmab.ch10.p1:
Held in hand, the Stone amplifies any transmutation: range and damage half again, no concentration, and the circle no longer rebounds from instability, misunderstood glyphs or exceeding your rank. Each transmutation costs it a soul, plus one per stage.

But it can be seen from afar: its bearer glows, and the monsters around come running.
treatise.fmab.ch10.p2:
A Stone is made only of lives. On a human transmutation circle, lay crystallized blood: the circle consumes everything alive in its area and condenses their souls. A villager is worth twelve souls, a beast three. The Stone cores homunculi leave behind, four melted around crystallized blood, make one too: those are lives, already taken.

It is the ultimate taboo.
treatise.fmab.ch10.p3: Karma keeps track of what you do. Sacrificing and killing villagers lower it; destroying homunculi, defending villagers and repairing raise it. Villagers talk about it: low karma raises their prices and sets their golems on you. Very low (−60), Lust comes once to make you Father's offer, without fighting. Right-click her to accept: a Stone core as an advance, your karma drops further, and the homunculi stop coming for you. Striking her, leaving her a minute without an answer or walking away means no: your karma rises a little, she attacks, and from then on a hostile homunculus comes hunting you now and then.
treatise.fmab.ch10.p4: Every eight days, around noon, the moon passes before the sun. During this eclipse, a Gate initiate holding a full Stone in each hand, on a human transmutation circle, becomes a Living Stone, like Hohenheim: the souls of both Stones, without limit, no more toll, no more concentration, and they rise from every death (twenty souls); their souls feed them, they no longer need to eat, and they regain a heart every second: as long as souls remain, they are in theory immortal. Sneaking and bare-handed, they absorb the souls of the living by keeping a hand on them, faster and faster; another Living Stone loses its own one by one. At zero, it all ends. And the homunculi hunt them.
treatise.fmab.ch10.p5:
A Living Stone no longer waits for anything: no pause between two claps, no recharge for the gauntlet or Scar's arm, no concentration to recover; a hand kept on a circle brings it to its full measure at once.

Projectiles aimed at a Living Stone come apart before they reach it: arrows, tridents, fireballs, even bullets. Their matter ends up in the Stone's pockets, element by element; whatever has no recipe comes back as it is.
treatise.fmab.ch10.gate:
The Stone and the Gate. A human transmutation with a Stone in hand lets you choose.

Open the Gate: the Truth takes its toll, then offers a deal. Every part it took can be bought back with the souls of your Stones (the body 60, sight 30, an arm 25, a leg 20, the organs 15). Talk to it to reopen the deal. Anywhere else, the Stone gives nothing back.

Create a being: a complete body of ingredients and one soul from the Stone, and the body lives, in the form you choose (a human being, a dog, a cat, a horse, a parrot); a beast bonds with you. The Gate stays shut; but that soul was someone's.

A Gate initiate claps even with a Stone between their palms.
treatise.fmab.ch11.title: The Promised Day
treatise.fmab.ch11.p1: Under Central, at the end of Sloth's tunnel, a door is sealed by the Ouroboros. It opens only for one who has seen the city's three guardians fall: Sloth, Wrath and Pride. Behind it, a shaft plunges to the throne room of Father, the original Homunculus, seated at the heart of the national transmutation circle.
treatise.fmab.ch11.p2: Around Father, in his throne room, Amestrian alchemy stops answering: he drains the tectonic energy it feeds on. No circle, no glove, no Stone. He changes form three times: the old man makes stone burst under his enemies; the faceless form forges a small, slow sun: take cover behind a pillar, or hit it back; the unstable divine form devours the souls around it to hold together, and comes apart if deprived of them. He tears the souls out of Living Stones.
treatise.fmab.ch11.p3: Xing's alkahestry draws on the dragon's pulse, which flows everywhere: Father cannot stop it. In jungles and cherry groves, May Chang teaches it to the good-hearted. Throw five kunai around an area: they draw a circle that heals your own, or traps and wounds your enemies (sneak and right-click to choose).
treatise.fmab.ch11.p4: In the north, in the snowy mountains, Fort Briggs bars the pass facing Drachma, whose soldiers prowl at the foot of the wall at night. General Olivier Armstrong recognizes her allies by their deeds, and entrusts them with a Briggs sabre: a heavy blade that bites deeper into homunculi, and owes nothing to alchemy.
treatise.fmab.ch11.p5: The national circle holds through its blood crests, left by Amestris's massacres: fields of ruins where blood still beats (cartographers sell maps to them). Plant an alkahestry kunai there, or carve a counter-circle with a chisel if you are a State Alchemist. While the circle holds, every eclipse is a Promised Day: Father's zone doubles, and he regenerates. Seal seven crests, and the circle breaks: his zone collapses.
treatise.fmab.ch8.p5:
The first time Truth takes the whole body, the soul at once finds itself in an iron armor, bound by a blood seal drawn inside the breastplate. The armor is hollow: only it can be seen. The soul neither hungers nor breathes, and does not eat. Blows wear the pieces: a piece that gives way can be made again (without a helm you see poorly, without greaves you walk poorly). Crouching, the soul transmutes the material it holds into its armor (an iron ingot for iron) and mends it.

If the breastplate gives way, the seal is erased: the soul goes back to wander before its Gate. Opening the Gate again is not so bad: Truth tears the seal away, but the soul draws it again on the way back, inside its armor, which comes out battered.

gate.fmab.pulled_severe: Something was missing. The circle tears open, and the black arms take all of you…
gate.fmab.choice.title: The Philosopher's Stone
gate.fmab.choice.text: The circle wakes, the Stone burns between your fingers (%s souls). Open your Gate, and buy back what the Truth took from you? Or give a soul from the Stone to the body born of the circle, so that it lives?
gate.fmab.choice.declined: You pull your hands away: the circle goes dark.
gate.fmab.choice.form: What form should the body born of the circle take? A soul from the Stone will bring it to life; a beast will bond with you.

gate.fmab.being.no_stone: You must hold the Stone to give one of its souls.
gate.fmab.being.created: The body breathes. It opens its eyes: it lives, with someone else's soul.
gate.fmab.knowledge_learned: Behind the Gate, all knowledge: you understand %s more glyphs.
gate.fmab.initiated: You have seen the Gate: you are now a %s. Join your hands (Shift + gloves key) to transmute without a circle.
gate.fmab.soul.first_armor: You open your eyes inside an iron armor. A blood seal holds you there.
gate.fmab.soul.notes: Your notebook now holds your blood seal and the circle that mends your armor (Iron and Repair).
gate.fmab.soul.piece_broken: A piece of your armor gives way: make it again.
gate.fmab.soul.no_armor: Lay an armor on the circle: a breastplate at least.
gate.fmab.soul.nobody: No soul is waiting for this circle.
gate.fmab.soul.summoned: A voice calls you. You wake up inside an armor.
gate.fmab.soul.summoned_other: %s's soul now dwells in the armor.
gate.fmab.soul.no_anchor: None of your seals answers. Someone will have to draw your soul circle.
truth.fmab.toll.seal: "You have no body left to give me. So I will take the seal."
gate.fmab.soul.seal_redrawn: Truth tears your seal away. You draw it again inside your armor on the way back: it comes out battered.
gate.fmab.seal_erased: The blood seal is erased. Your armor collapses, and your soul returns before the Gate…
truth.fmab.opening: "This is your Gate. You knocked: it opens."
truth.fmab.reclaim: Truth: "Where do you think you are going? You have no body left to leave with."
truth.fmab.bargain.offer: The Truth: "Well, you brought money. Souls… I will give back what you want, if you pay."
truth.fmab.bargain.title: Bargain with the Truth
truth.fmab.bargain.text: Every part it took from you can be bought back with the souls of your Stones.
truth.fmab.bargain.done: The Truth: "Deal. Come back whenever you like; I have all the time in the world."
truth.fmab.knowledge: "You wanted to see the Truth? I will show it to you."
automail.fmab.no_lost_arm: You are not missing an arm.
automail.fmab.no_lost_leg: You are not missing a leg.
automail.fmab.fitted: The nerves connect in a flash of pain: the automail replaces %s.
automail.fmab.broke: The automail replacing %s stopped working: have Winry repair it.
automail.fmab.blade_out: A blade springs from your automail forearm.
automail.fmab.blade_in: The blade withdraws: your arm takes back its shape.
homunculus.fmab.envy_reveals: "You thought you knew me?" The face comes apart: it is Envy.
homunculus.fmab.greed_wants: Greed: "I want everything! Money, women, power… What are you offering me?" (%s gold ingots' worth: gold, emeralds, diamonds)
homunculus.fmab.greed_more: Greed: "That's it? Come back with %s of those."
homunculus.fmab.greed_pact: Greed: "Deal. I never lie." He follows you, as long as you pay him (a gold ingot or an emerald a day).
homunculus.fmab.greed_yields: Greed: "Not bad. I respect those who put me down. Talk to me, we can make a deal."
homunculus.fmab.greed_ally: Greed: "As long as you pay, boss."
homunculus.fmab.greed_leaves: Greed: "No gold, no Greed." The pact is broken.
homunculus.fmab.wrath_eye: His Ultimate Eye saw the blow coming.
homunculus.fmab.pride_reveals: The child smiles. His shadow rises, full of eyes and teeth: it is Pride.

block.fmab.father_seal.opens: The serpent lets go of its tail: the seal dissolves. A cold breath rises from the depths.
homunculus.fmab.father_phase1: Father rises. His face fades away; a small sun is born between his hands.
homunculus.fmab.father_phase2: Father absorbs more than he can hold. His divine form cracks; he needs souls to hold together.
homunculus.fmab.father_falls: Father's Stone runs dry. Behind him, the Gate opens: "You wanted to rise? I am taking you back where you belong."
homunculus.fmab.father_drains: Father tears %s souls out of you.

item.fmab.kunai.mode_heal: The kunai will draw a healing circle.
item.fmab.kunai.mode_trap: The kunai will draw a trap circle.
entity.fmab.drachma_general.rally: The Drachman General raises his sabre: "Guards, to me! No Amestrian leaves this place!"
entity.fmab.slicer.younger: The body's seal fades, but the helmet holds: "Big brother!" The younger one takes over the armor.
entity.fmab.kimblee.taunt: Kimblee presses his palms together: "Listen. The most beautiful sound in the world is an explosion."
npc.fmab.mustang.line1: Mustang: "Colonel Mustang, the Flame Alchemist. A snap of the fingers, and oxygen does the rest."
npc.fmab.mustang.line2: Mustang: "One day I'll be Führer. And every woman in the army will wear a miniskirt."
npc.fmab.mustang.line3: Mustang: "Hughes... I won't let his death go unanswered."
npc.fmab.mustang.line4: Mustang: "My gloves are for sale, as long as you know not to get them wet."
npc.fmab.hawkeye.line1: Hawkeye: "Lieutenant Hawkeye. I cover the Colonel. He tends to expose himself."
npc.fmab.hawkeye.line2: Hawkeye: "A gun doesn't think. That's the job of whoever holds it."
npc.fmab.hawkeye.line3: Hawkeye: "On rainy days, stay close to him. He's useless."
npc.fmab.armstrong.line1: Armstrong: "Alex Louis Armstrong, the Strong Arm Alchemist! This art has been passed down the Armstrong line for generations!"
npc.fmab.armstrong.line2: Armstrong takes off his shirt: "Behold these muscles, forged by discipline!"
npc.fmab.armstrong.line3: Armstrong sheds a tear: "What a touching story!"
npc.fmab.armstrong.line4: Armstrong: "My sister commands Briggs. Don't tell her I cry."
npc.fmab.hughes.line1: Hughes hands you a photo: "My daughter Elicia! She's three, look how cute she is!"
npc.fmab.hughes.line2: Hughes: "The Investigations Office knows a lot of things. Too many, sometimes."
npc.fmab.hughes.line3: Hughes: "Roy will become Führer. Someone has to push him."
npc.fmab.hughes.line4: Hughes: "Something is wrong with this country. The pattern of the massacres... it's no accident."
npc.fmab.ling.line1: Ling: "Ling Yao, twelfth prince of Xing. I'm looking for the stone that grants immortality. And food, if you have any."
npc.fmab.ling.line2: Ling: "A king exists for his people. Not the other way around."
npc.fmab.ling.line3: Ling: "My kunai and blades come from Xing. Nothing better this side of the desert."
npc.fmab.lan_fan.line1: Lan Fan, behind her mask: "I protect the young master. Don't come too close."
npc.fmab.lan_fan.line2: Lan Fan moves her automail arm: "I gave up my arm for him. I'd do it again."
npc.fmab.lan_fan.line3: Lan Fan: "Knives, if you know how to throw them."
npc.fmab.alphonse.line1: Alphonse, a child's voice inside the armor: "Hello! My brother's around somewhere, probably angry about someone calling him short again."
npc.fmab.alphonse.line2: Alphonse: "We tried to bring our mother back. Nothing is equivalent to a life."
npc.fmab.alphonse.line3: Alphonse: "I can't feel heat or cold. But I remember the taste of Mom's pies."
npc.fmab.alphonse.line4: Alphonse: "One is all, all is one. If you're starting out, these tomes will help."
npc.fmab.pinako.line1: Pinako puffs on her pipe: "A Rockbell automail costs you, but it lasts a lifetime."
npc.fmab.pinako.line2: Pinako: "Those two Elric brats burned down their house so they couldn't turn back."
npc.fmab.pinako.line3: Pinako: "Winry's in Rush Valley. She has my talent, and her mother's temper."
npc.fmab.basque_grand.line1: Grand: "Brigadier General Grand, the Iron Blood Alchemist. Steel obeys the army."
npc.fmab.basque_grand.line2: Grand: "Ishval? An order is an order. I don't ask questions."
npc.fmab.basque_grand.line3: Grand: "Iron, blades. Everything you need to hold a position."
npc.fmab.mcdougal.line1: McDougal: "The Freezing Alchemist. The body is made of water; I only have to freeze it."
npc.fmab.mcdougal.line2: McDougal: "I saw what the army did here. I will never forgive it."
npc.fmab.mcdougal.line3: McDougal: "Ice, for the State examination. Candidates always run short."

npc.fmab.tattooist.line2: The tattooist: "Alchemical ink, thread, paint: everything you need to carry a circle on you."
npc.fmab.tattooist.line3: The tattooist: "Ishvalans tattooed their circles long before Amestris. Scar wears one on his arm."
npc.fmab.ishvalan.line1: The Ishvalan: "Ishvala created the world. Alchemy unmakes and remakes it: a sacrilege, our priests said."
npc.fmab.ishvalan.line2: The Ishvalan: "Scar's brother studied Xing's alchemy. He said breaking down and rebuilding are the two hands of a single gesture."
npc.fmab.ishvalan.line3: The Ishvalan: "We rebuild with the earth of our ruins. It remembers our houses."
npc.fmab.ishvalan.line4: The Ishvalan: "Our tomes, our dyes, our terracotta: it's all the war left us."
npc.fmab.tucker.line1: Tucker: "Shou Tucker, the Sewing-Life Alchemist. My first talking chimera earned me my license."
npc.fmab.tucker.line2: Tucker: "The annual assessment is coming. I need a new result. Any result."
npc.fmab.tucker.line3: Tucker smiles for too long: "Nina and Alexander are playing in the other room."

treatise.fmab.ch12.title: Bestiary
treatise.fmab.ch12.p1: Amestrian soldiers guard Central and Fort Briggs. They mean you no harm while your karma stays honest; strike one of them, or fall too low, and the whole garrison hunts you. They cut down any monster that comes near.
treatise.fmab.ch12.p2: A haunted armor is a soul bound by a blood seal to an empty suit. Struck down, it falls to pieces; while the seal holds, it reforms. While it lies there, erase the seal with a right-click. Barry the Chopper, above Laboratory 5, is one of them, bigger and crueler. When he raises his cleaver (the ground in front of him turns red), back off or get behind him: the blow sweeps the whole arc before him and knocks you down. Wounded by half, he lowers his head and charges once; dodge him against a wall and he knocks himself out. His seal holds the first time he falls: he gets up a few seconds later, and you must strike him down a second time to erase it.
treatise.fmab.ch12.p3: Immortal soldiers, made beneath Central, regenerate endlessly and get back up once struck down. Fire, the Briggs sabre or alkahestry finish them for good.
treatise.fmab.ch12.p4: Chimeras come out of the army's laboratories and prowl at night: the big one, lion, snake and goat, rears before it strikes and poisons; the crawling one climbs walls and its bite weakens.

treatise.fmab.ch13.p1: Scar's arm unites alchemy and alkahestry, but keeps only decomposition. Engraved from his brother's notes, it turns to dust, bare-handed, the block or creature it strikes; it does not fear Father's zone.
treatise.fmab.ch13.p2: Kimblee transmutes matter into explosives. His crimson seals turn a block into a mine, which blows when a creature passes or when you clap your hands (sneaking). Mustang snaps his fingers instead: his spark gloves reach far, but rain makes them useless.
treatise.fmab.ch13.p3: Riza Hawkeye does without alchemy: pistol and sniper rifle, one cartridge per shot. A bullet weakens with distance, and barely slows a homunculus down: its Stone closes the wound. King Bradley still sees the bullets coming. Maes Hughes throws his knives, light and cheap.
treatise.fmab.ch13.p4: Ling Yao's Xing sword is fast: chain blows without pause, each strikes harder than the last. Sneaking with the sword in hand, you sense the qi of everything alive nearby, even through walls.

item.fmab.xerxes_mural.text1: An aging king, turned towards a flask where a black shadow stirs. Around the flask, alchemists in prayer.
item.fmab.xerxes_mural.text2: A slave, number 23, at the flask's side. The shadow speaks to him; it gives him a name: Hohenheim.
item.fmab.xerxes_mural.text3: Soldiers dig a great circle around the whole kingdom, at night, in secret, on the shadow's orders.
item.fmab.xerxes_mural.text4: The circle lights up. Everyone falls, except two figures at the center: one takes the other's face.
item.fmab.xerxes_mural.text5: A lone man walks west, filled with the souls of a whole people. Behind him, the city is nothing but dust.

npc.fmab.hohenheim.line1: Hohenheim: "I was slave number 23. He was the one who gave me a name."
npc.fmab.hohenheim.line2: Hohenheim: "One night was enough for Xerxes to vanish. I still carry every one of them."
npc.fmab.hohenheim.line3: Hohenheim: "He wants to do to Amestris what he did to Xerxes, to swallow the Truth itself."
npc.fmab.hohenheim.line4: Hohenheim: "Equivalent exchange is not a law. It is a promise we make to ourselves."

treatise.fmab.ch14.title: Lands of Amestris
treatise.fmab.ch14.p1: Liore, in the desert: Father Cornello performs "miracles" there in Leto's name. An Alchemist recognizes a transmutation, made with an impure red stone, also found under his temple's altar. It amplifies, but holds nothing.
treatise.fmab.ch14.p2: The ruins of Ishval bear a blood crest. Scar wanders there: he hunts State Alchemists, but entrusts the others, if their heart is true, with his brother's notes.
treatise.fmab.ch14.p3: The ruins of Xerxes, a kingdom gone in one night, keep murals of its fall. Van Hohenheim, the only survivor, sometimes returns there.
treatise.fmab.ch14.p4: In Dublith, among the southern plains and forests, Izumi Curtis runs a butcher shop with her husband. That is where you become her student. Her last trial takes place on Yock Island, in the middle of the sea, and she gives you its map: hold out there ten minutes straight without leaving.
cinematic.fmab.promised_day.sub: The sun goes dark. The national circle awakens.
cinematic.fmab.father_fall.sub: "You wanted to rise? I am taking you back where you belong."
cinematic.fmab.nina.1: In the back room, a chimera lies on the floor. It has long brown fur, like Alexander, the family dog.
cinematic.fmab.nina.2: It raises its head, and it speaks. Its voice is that of a little girl.
cinematic.fmab.nina.3: Tucker kept his title two years running. For his first talking chimera, he used his wife. This year, he used Nina.
cinematic.fmab.nina.4: "An alchemist must never forget what he transmutes." That night, it rained on Central.

cinematic.fmab.epilogue.1: The national circle has fallen silent. Beneath Central, Father's throne is an empty hall, and daylight has returned to Amestris.
cinematic.fmab.epilogue.2: The immortal soldiers have collapsed, and the souls of the Stone have gone home, one by one.
cinematic.fmab.epilogue.3: In Resembool, a tree was planted by Trisha's grave. Pinako says it looks like someone.
cinematic.fmab.epilogue.4: In Ishval, they rebuild. At Briggs, they still keep watch. In Xing, they speak of an emperor who kept his word.
cinematic.fmab.epilogue.5: Alchemy keeps teaching what it always has: nothing is gained without giving something in return.
cinematic.fmab.epilogue.6: And somewhere, an alchemist looks at an engraved watch, and does not forget.

treatise.fmab.ch1.places:
Finding your way: village cartographers sell maps to Central, Resembool, Dublith, Rush Valley and many other places; Izumi, the examiner, May Chang and Hohenheim hand some out too. Advancements (L key) trace the alchemist's path.

Concentration grows with rank: 20 for an Apprentice, 40 for an Alchemist, 70 for a State Alchemist, 120 for a Gate Initiate. Crouching still, you recover it faster.
treatise.fmab.ch1.path:
The alchemist's path.

1. Draw your first circles (“The three steps”). Each successful transmutation trains its school; at 60 mastery points in all, you become an Alchemist.

2. Visit Izumi Curtis in Dublith early: her trials only count once you are her student.

3. Once an Alchemist, take the State examination at Central HQ. First succeed with a two-stage circle (“Thinking in stages”), bring a transmuted weapon (stone lance or arm blade), 8 blocks of ice or snow and 4 iron ingots, then defeat the golem. The examiner then sends you to Laboratory 5.

4. Crystallized blood, needed for a Philosopher's Stone, is found at blood crests and in Gluttony's Belly.

treatise.fmab.ch2.objects:
Making an object follows the same steps.

1. Understand: lay the object on a circle of its main element (Iron for an iron pickaxe, Earth for a stone one) with Decompose. It breaks down into its matter, and you learn how it is made.

2. Then think of the object (design page, J key), or lay one as a model, on a Recompose circle of the same element, with the matter it holds, on the circle or on you.

3. The object comes out new. The exchange is equivalent; extra matter of the main element laid on the circle makes it sturdier. With a Philosopher's Stone, no matter is needed. Gold, however, is never made.

Recompose is an Alchemist's glyph: drawn by an Apprentice, the circle may rebound.
treatise.fmab.ch2.tomes:
The tomes and their glyphs.

Rudiments: Earth, Water, Fix, Project. On Stone and Metal: Iron, Copper, Decompose, Repair. On Wood and Fiber: Wood, Fiber. On Living Matter: Plant, Flesh. Librarians sell these first tomes.

On Carbon and Crystals: Carbon, Crystal. On Sulfur and Lime: Sulfur, Lime. Forms: Recompose, Direction, Intensity. On the Planetary Metals: Silver, Tin, Lead, Mercury. On the Deep Metals: Zinc, Nickel, Aluminium, Netherite. Notes on Combustion: Fire, Air. More experienced librarians keep them.

Hohenheim's notes (Human) are found only in Resembool; the alchemy of gold (Gold), only in forbidden ruins.
